Durable context for whoever — or whatever — picks this up next. Kept as an issue rather than in an agent's local memory so it survives a cleared context and is visible to everyone.

## How this repository is being worked

Changes go through the [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md) workflow end to end: branch, implement, ui-review, verifier, code-review, PR. PRs merge when CI is green. Findings become issues. The loop continues to the next item without pausing for step-by-step approval.

The point is that it runs unattended, so stopping to confirm each step defeats it.

## What still gets surfaced rather than decided silently

Proceeding by default does not mean deciding everything. Three categories get a recommendation and a question:

1. **Changes to what users see** — image quality, layout tradeoffs. #96 is the live example: re-encoding to WebP is well-measured, but q82/600px is a judgment about acceptable fidelity, not a fact.
2. **Changes to other contributors' behavior** — #147 committed tool config that runs hooks on anyone's machine who clones. That deserved saying out loud, not just doing.
3. **Rewrites of shared history** — never silently. See the note below on why this keeps coming up.

The rest of the work does not wait on those answers. Finish everything that does not depend on the decision first, then ask.

## Two things that have repeatedly caught people out

**Checks that run without asserting on what they produced.** This is the repo's signature defect, found three separate times: the E2E smoke passed against a chat service returning `fallback: true`; the seed ran green on every PR while writing credentials that could never authenticate (#141); a category page referenced an image that had never existed (#137). A green check is not evidence unless something inspects its output.

**Verifying in a richer environment than the real one.** Also recurring: a populated local venv vs CI's bare one; jsdom vs a real browser; three sampled viewports vs the breakpoint boundaries where the defects actually live; `node_modules` vs the standalone image; a local stack reading `.env` vs CI with none. If a check passes locally, confirm it runs in the environment that matters.

**Deleting files does not shrink `git clone`.** The blobs stay reachable from history. #146 removed 68.6 MB from the working tree and the web image; `size-pack` did not move. Worth remembering before promising a clone-size win — see the measurement in #66.

## Running the stack locally

Environments differ per machine (port collisions, whether Ollama is installed for `LLM_PROVIDER=local`). `make e2e-smoke` may need a compose override for ports and provider. Resolve collisions with an override file using `ports: !override` — a plain `ports:` list appends rather than replaces — and never by stopping containers you did not start.

## Current state

`main` is clean. #145, #146 and #147 are merged. Open: #96 (WebP re-encode, the next substantive item), #66 (image weight, parent of #96), #118 (import-declaration guardrail), #129 (chat panel below `sm`, needs a design decision), #69 and #90 (blocked upstream).

Hit repeatedly while working #196 and #216, and worth writing down because it silently costs a review pass every time.

## What happens

`npx next dev` on a free port, click the launcher, and nothing opens:

```
launcher visible: true
#chat: 0   dialog: 0   aside/section: 0
launcher still there: 1
pageerrors: (none)
```

Reproduced on two independently started dev servers. Against a composed production stack the same click opens the panel and `chat-controls.spec.ts` passes 2/2, so this is `next dev` specifically, not the code being broken.

React *is* hydrated on the dev server — a controlled input on `/contact` keeps its typed value, and `window.next` is present — so this is not a general hydration failure. It is this component.

## Likely mechanism

`apps/web/src/components/chat.tsx:217-230` closes the panel whenever focus moves outside the widget:

```ts
const onFocusIn = (event: FocusEvent) => {
  const target = event.target as Node | null
  if (target && widgetRef.current?.contains(target)) return
  closedByFocusOut.current = true
  setShowChat(false)
}
```

Opening the panel unmounts the launcher (#190), so the focused element disappears and focus falls to `document.body`. `body` is not inside `widgetRef`, so the handler closes the panel again. In a production build the panel's own autofocus wins that race; under dev — where React 19's StrictMode mounts effects, tears them down and mounts them again — it does not.

That last sentence is the part I have not proven. The behaviour is reproducible; the StrictMode explanation is the most likely cause and is untested. `reactStrictMode` is not set in `next.config.js`, so it defaults on.

## Why it matters more than it looks

Every chat journey is unrunnable locally without standing up docker. That is documented in `playwright.config.ts` as "these journeys cross web, chat and the database", which is true of the *message* path but not of this: opening a panel needs no backend. The real reason is this bug, and the comment hides it.

It also means `ui-review` cannot see the chat panel on a dev server, so any review of chat UI silently falls back to reading source. That happened twice today.

## Worth checking as part of a fix

Whether a focus landing on `document.body` should close the panel at all. `relatedTarget === null` or a `body` target is the browser losing focus rather than the user moving it somewhere, which is the same distinction the comment above that effect already draws for the address bar.

Found while wiring `/profile` into the field-boundary guard for #220. It looked like a Playwright race for four attempts; it is contention, and it affects real visitors.

## Measured

Against the composed production stack with a cold image cache, at 1440x900:

1. Land on `/`. It requests twenty product images through the optimiser at once — `GET /_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2F<n>%2F<uuid>.webp&w=384&q=75`.
2. Issue any further navigation.

```
still-pending after 21s:  20 x /_next/image?...&w=384&q=75
waitForLoadState('networkidle'):  never reached within 120s
GET /profile issued at 6.6s -> no response, aborted by the client at 36.6s
```

The same route is fast when nothing else is in flight: signed-out `/profile` answers in **6.9ms**, `/` in 6.5ms, `/login` in 5.5ms. So this is not the route being slow — it is the optimiser saturating the server and everything else queueing behind it.

## Why it matters outside the tests

A first-time visitor lands on the home page and gets exactly this: twenty optimisations, and any click during them queued behind. The cache warms afterwards, so it is invisible on a second visit and on any machine that has already loaded the page — which is why nothing has caught it.

Twenty is the whole first screen: `apps/web/src/app/page.tsx` renders every seeded product per category, and #171 sized them to `w=384` at this width, so all twenty are distinct optimiser jobs on first paint.

## Related, and probably the same root

- **#66** — `public/images` is 732 MB. The bigger the source, the longer each optimisation takes.
- **#180** — the category grid's `priority` cutoff already showed the optimiser is a contended resource, with adjacent cards arriving 2.7s apart.

Both of those treat the optimiser as slow. This is the sharper version: it is slow enough to block *unrelated navigations*, not just other images.

## What the test does instead, and why it is not the fix

`e2e/form-fields.spec.ts` aborts `**/_next/image**` for the duration of its sign-in transit, since none of the fields it measures is an image. That takes the profile surfaces from 4+ minutes of timeouts to 38 seconds. It is a workaround inside one spec and it deliberately hides this — worth remembering if anyone tries to reproduce from there.

## Worth checking as part of a fix

Whether the optimiser's concurrency is configurable, whether the seeded sources are simply too large to resize at request time (#66), and whether the home page needs twenty products above the fold at all.

**The PR queue is stale and one PR is permanently red.** All 5 open PRs are Dependabot, all from Aug 10 (4 days old):

That is exactly issue **#69** ("Revisit ESLint 10 when eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y supports it") — known-blocked upstream. The cause is that `.github/dependabot.yml` gives the `eslint` group patterns but **no `update-types` filter**, so it pulls majors that the config's own comment says should stay ungrouped. It will regenerate this same red PR every Monday until that's fixed.

**The issue backlog is ~46 items, heavily one flavour.** Roughly 21 are accessibility/visual-polish findings (contrast, focus indicators, alt text, announcements), 8 are image-delivery/performance, and the rest are tooling and runbook gaps. The a11y cluster is where the recent merged work has been (#221, #229, #234, #236, #239, #242, #244) — it's productive, but it's also the well-trodden path.

**1. Drain the PR queue** — merge the four green ones, close #223, and fix the Dependabot `eslint` group to minor/patch only so it stops resurfacing. Small, closes a recurring false alarm, and clears the board. (~30 min)

**3. #228 — the chat panel can't be opened under `next dev`.** A force multiplier rather than a user-facing fix: right now every chat journey needs a full docker stack, so `ui-review` silently falls back to reading source for chat UI. """Guard each Dependabot version hold against the upstream fact that justifies it.

An `ignore` entry in `.github/dependabot.yml` is a claim about the outside world:
that a resolver cannot install the upgrade. Claims like that expire silently. The
upstream project ships support, the hold keeps suppressing the pull request, and
the repository sits on an old major with nothing to say so.

Two assertions, catching two different mistakes:

- `test_next_eslint_major_is_still_unsupported_upstream` measures the fact. It
  reads the peer range `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` actually declares in the web
  lockfile and fails once that range admits the next ESLint major -- the signal
  to delete the hold and let the `eslint` group carry the upgrade.
- `test_config_holds_the_eslint_major` measures the declaration, and only the
  declaration. It catches the hold being dropped while the block is still real,
  which is what reopens the unmergeable weekly pull request (#223).

Nothing here catches Dependabot misreading the config; that is only observable
from a Dependabot run. `yaml` is deliberately not imported: CI's script-test job
builds a bare virtualenv, so a third-party import passes locally and fails there.
"""

import json
import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DEPENDABOT_CONFIG = REPO_ROOT / ".github/dependabot.yml"
WEB_LOCKFILE = REPO_ROOT / "apps/web/package-lock.json"

ESLINT_PACKAGE = "node_modules/eslint"
BLOCKING_PLUGIN = "node_modules/eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y"


def lockfile_packages() -> dict:
    return json.loads(WEB_LOCKFILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("packages", {})


def installed_major(package: str) -> int:
    version = lockfile_packages().get(package, {}).get("version", "")
    match = re.match(r"(\d+)\.", version)
    if not match:
        raise AssertionError(f"no parseable version for {package} in {WEB_LOCKFILE}")
    return int(match.group(1))


def peer_range(package: str, peer: str) -> str:
    return lockfile_packages().get(package, {}).get("peerDependencies", {}).get(peer, "")


def admitted_majors(spec: str) -> set[int]:
    """Major versions a `^3 || ^4 || >=8` style range admits.

    Deliberately narrow: it understands the comparators this peer range actually
    uses. An unrecognised range yields no majors, which fails the vacuity guard
    below rather than quietly reporting the major as blocked.
    """
    majors = set()
    for token in spec.split("||"):
        token = token.strip()
        caret = re.fullmatch(r"\^(\d+)(?:\.\d+)*", token)
        if caret:
            majors.add(int(caret.group(1)))
            continue
        exact = re.fullmatch(r"(\d+)(?:\.[\dx*]+)*", token)
        if exact:
            majors.add(int(exact.group(1)))
    return majors


def eslint_hold_block() -> str:
    """The lines of the `eslint` ignore entry, or "" when there is no such entry."""
    lines = DEPENDABOT_CONFIG.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if re.fullmatch(r'\s*-\s*dependency-name:\s*"?eslint"?\s*', line):
            indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
            block = [line]
            for following in lines[index + 1 :]:
                if following.strip() and (len(following) - len(following.lstrip())) <= indent:
                    break
                block.append(following)
            return "\n".join(block)
    return ""


class EslintMajorHoldTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_blocking_peer_range_is_readable(self):
        """Vacuity guard: a rename or a lockfile shape change empties both claims."""
        spec = peer_range(BLOCKING_PLUGIN, "eslint")
        self.assertTrue(
            spec, f"{BLOCKING_PLUGIN} declares no eslint peer range in {WEB_LOCKFILE}"
        )
        self.assertTrue(
            admitted_majors(spec),
            f"no major version parsed out of {BLOCKING_PLUGIN} peer range {spec!r}",
        )

    def test_next_eslint_major_is_still_unsupported_upstream(self):
        blocked = installed_major(ESLINT_PACKAGE) + 1
        spec = peer_range(BLOCKING_PLUGIN, "eslint")
        self.assertNotIn(
            blocked,
            admitted_majors(spec),
            f"eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y now peers on eslint {blocked} (range {spec!r}). "
            f"The hold in {DEPENDABOT_CONFIG} is stale -- remove it and #69, and let "
            f"the eslint group carry the major.",
        )

    def test_config_holds_the_eslint_major(self):
        block = eslint_hold_block()
        self.assertTrue(
            block,
            f"{DEPENDABOT_CONFIG} has no ignore entry for eslint, so Dependabot will "
            f"reopen the ESLint major every week while it cannot install (#223).",
        )
        self.assertIn("version-update:semver-major", block)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

gh issue create --title "eslint-config-next is grouped with eslint, so it tracks the wrong release train" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Found while adding the Dependabot hold that stops #223 reopening.

## What is wrong

`.github/dependabot.yml` puts `eslint-config-next` in the `eslint` group, because the group's `eslint-*` pattern matches it:

```yaml
      eslint:
        patterns:
          - "eslint"
          - "eslint-*"
          - "@typescript-eslint/*"
```

But `eslint-config-next` is published from the Next.js repository and carries Next's version numbers, not ESLint's. It versions in lockstep with `next`, which is the `next` group.

## Measured

`#225` merged `next` 16.2.12 -> 16.3.0. After that merge, on `main`:

```
$ grep -nE '"next"|eslint-config-next' apps/web/package.json
22:    "next": "16.3.0",
44:    "eslint-config-next": "16.2.12",
```

The two are now a minor apart. #223 is the confirming evidence in the other direction: it bundled `eslint` 9->10 *and* `eslint-config-next` 16.2.12->16.3.0 into one pull request, which is only possible if they share a group.

So while the ESLint major was unmergeable, `eslint-config-next` could not advance either -- it was held hostage by an unrelated blocker in the same group.

## Why this is not urgent

The hold added for #69 unblocks it: with the ESLint major ignored, the `eslint` group's next run proposes `eslint-config-next` 16.3.0 on its own, which resolves against `eslint@9`. The skew closes by itself on the next Dependabot run.

What remains is that the grouping is still wrong, so the same hostage situation returns the next time anything in the `eslint` group is blocked.

## Suggested fix

Add an exclude to the `eslint` group and an explicit pattern to the `next` group:

```yaml
      eslint:
        patterns:
          - "eslint"
          - "eslint-*"
          - "@typescript-eslint/*"
        exclude-patterns:
          - "eslint-config-next"
      next:
        patterns:
          - "next"
          - "@next/*"
          - "eslint-config-next"
```

`exclude-patterns` rather than reordering the groups: Dependabot assigns a dependency to the first group whose patterns match, so relying on declaration order makes the behaviour invisible to anyone reading the file.

The header comment's own principle -- "Package families must version in lockstep" -- is the argument for the move.

## Why it was not fixed at the time

The branch it came up on (`chore/dependabot-ignore-eslint-major`) is scoped to stopping the recurring unmergeable pull request. Regrouping a package is a separate decision about how upgrades arrive, and the skew it causes self-heals without it.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

`.github/dependabot.yml` appears in none of `detect_changed_surfaces.py`'s pattern lists -- not `RUNTIME_PATTERNS`, `WEB_PATTERNS`, `CHAT_PATTERNS`, or `DOC_PATTERNS`. Classifying a changeset containing only that file:

## Why it is not simply a bug

The fallback is the safe direction. An unrecognised path running too much is the failure mode you want, and it is presumably why the `unknown` branch exists at all.

What is worth deciding is whether this particular file should keep taking it. Two arguments pull against each other:

- **It changes no runtime code.** Nothing it touches can affect a rendered pixel or a served byte. On that reading it belongs with the docs surface, or a narrower gate of its own.
- **It changes what future upgrades look like.** A grouping or `ignore` edit decides which dependency pull requests arrive and how they are bundled -- and dependency upgrades are exactly the thing that *can* move rendering behaviour. On that reading the full gate is not obviously wrong.

There is also a third option: leave the routing alone and add the path to a pattern list purely so the classification is deliberate rather than incidental. Right now the behaviour is correct by accident, and nothing records that anyone chose it.

Decide which of the three the repository wants, then either add `.github/dependabot.yml` to a pattern list or write down in `scripts/detect_changed_surfaces.py` why it is deliberately unmatched. """Guard each Dependabot version hold against the upstream fact that justifies it.

An `ignore` entry in `.github/dependabot.yml` is a claim about the outside world:
that a resolver cannot install the upgrade. Claims like that expire silently. The
upstream project ships support, the hold keeps suppressing the pull request, and
the repository sits on an old major with nothing to say so.

Two assertions, catching two different mistakes:

- `test_next_eslint_major_is_still_unsupported_upstream` measures the fact. It
  reads every `eslint` peer range declared in the web lockfile and fails once
  none of them caps below the next major -- the signal to delete the hold, close
  #69, and delete this module.
- `test_config_holds_the_eslint_major` measures the declaration, and only the
  declaration. It catches the hold being dropped while the block is still real,
  which is what reopens the unmergeable weekly pull request (#223). It reads the
  hold out of the npm `/apps/web` entry specifically: a hold under one of the
  three `pip` entries would apply to the wrong dependency set while still
  reading, to an unscoped search, as present.

**The whole set, not one member.** Three packages cap ESLint below 10 today, and
`eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` is only the one named in #69. The other two are pinned
inside `eslint-config-next`, so bumping ESLint alone does not move them. Tracking
one would mean that when jsx-a11y ships support first, this suite says the hold
is stale while `npm install` still fails -- sending someone to reopen exactly the
pull request the hold exists to suppress.

**An unreadable range counts as not blocking.** `admitted_majors` understands the
comparators these ranges actually use and reports the rest as unparsed. A range
carrying an unparsed token cannot be shown to exclude the major, so it is not
counted as a blocker: an upstream that starts writing `>=10` or `^10.0.0-0` --
both already present in this lockfile for other packages -- moves the suite
toward failing loudly rather than toward holding on in silence.

What this cannot catch: Dependabot's own reading of the config, which is only
observable from a Dependabot run; and npm's real resolution, which this
approximates by skipping any package with its own nested `eslint`. Every package
declaring an `eslint` peer here resolves against the hoisted one today, so that
filter is currently a no-op kept for the case where it stops being one.

`yaml` is deliberately not imported: CI's script-test job builds a bare
virtualenv, so a third-party import passes locally and fails there.
"""

import json
import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DEPENDABOT_CONFIG = REPO_ROOT / ".github/dependabot.yml"
WEB_LOCKFILE = REPO_ROOT / "apps/web/package-lock.json"

ESLINT_PACKAGE = "node_modules/eslint"


def lockfile_packages() -> dict:
    return json.loads(WEB_LOCKFILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("packages", {})


def installed_major(package: str) -> int:
    version = lockfile_packages().get(package, {}).get("version", "")
    match = re.match(r"(\d+)\.", version)
    if not match:
        raise AssertionError(f"no parseable version for {package} in {WEB_LOCKFILE}")
    return int(match.group(1))


def eslint_peer_ranges() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Every package declaring an `eslint` peer that resolves against the hoisted one."""
    packages = lockfile_packages()
    ranges = {}
    for name, meta in packages.items():
        if not isinstance(meta, dict):
            continue
        peers = meta.get("peerDependencies")
        if not isinstance(peers, dict) or "eslint" not in peers:
            continue
        if f"{name}/node_modules/eslint" in packages:
            continue
        ranges[name] = peers["eslint"]
    return ranges


def admitted_majors(spec: str) -> tuple[set[int], list[str]]:
    """Major versions a `^3 || ^4` style range admits, and the tokens not understood.

    Deliberately narrow. Returning the failures rather than dropping them is the
    point: a caller that treats "did not parse" as "does not admit" would let the
    hold outlive an upstream that changed comparator style.
    """
    majors: set[int] = set()
    unparsed: list[str] = []
    for token in spec.split("||"):
        token = token.strip()
        if not token:
            continue
        caret = re.fullmatch(r"\^(\d+)(?:\.\d+)*", token)
        if caret:
            majors.add(int(caret.group(1)))
            continue
        exact = re.fullmatch(r"(\d+)(?:\.[\dx*]+)*", token)
        if exact:
            majors.add(int(exact.group(1)))
            continue
        unparsed.append(token)
    return majors, unparsed


def blockers(major: int) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Packages whose declared peer range demonstrably excludes `major`."""
    blocking = {}
    for name, spec in eslint_peer_ranges().items():
        majors, unparsed = admitted_majors(spec)
        if unparsed or not majors:
            continue
        if major not in majors:
            blocking[name] = spec
    return blocking


def update_entry(ecosystem: str, directory: str) -> list[str]:
    """The lines of one `updates:` entry, selected by ecosystem and directory.

    The hold has to sit in the entry that actually builds `apps/web`. Scoping by
    ecosystem alone is not enough -- this file carries three separate `pip`
    entries -- and an unscoped search would accept a hold placed under any of
    them, which Dependabot would apply to the wrong dependency set.
    """
    lines = DEPENDABOT_CONFIG.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    starts = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if "- package-ecosystem:" in line]
    for position, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        entry = lines[start:end]
        body = "\n".join(entry)
        if f'package-ecosystem: "{ecosystem}"' in body and f'directory: "{directory}"' in body:
            return entry
    return []


def eslint_hold_block() -> str:
    """The lines of the `eslint` ignore entry, or "" when there is no such entry."""
    lines = update_entry("npm", "/apps/web")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if re.fullmatch(r'\s*-\s*dependency-name:\s*"?eslint"?\s*', line):

chore(deps): hold the ESLint major that cannot install

Dependabot reopened the same unmergeable pull request every Monday. It
proposes ESLint 9 -> 10 for apps/web, and three packages peer on eslint
with a range that stops at 9, so npm fails with ERESOLVE before any lint
rule runs. #223 is the pull request; Web App CI failed on exactly that.

The obvious fix -- capping the eslint group at minor and patch -- would
not have worked. `update-types` inside a group controls only whether an
update joins that group, not whether Dependabot proposes it, so the
major would still have arrived every week, just ungrouped. An `ignore`
is what actually stops it, and it keeps the group free to carry the
major in lockstep once it can install.

The hold is a claim about the outside world, and claims like that expire
silently: upstream ships support, the hold keeps suppressing the pull
request, and nothing says so. So it comes with a guard that measures the
fact rather than the config -- it reads every eslint peer range declared
in the web lockfile and fails once none of them caps below the next
major, which is the signal to remove the hold, close #69, and delete the
guard with them.

It measures all of them, not jsx-a11y alone. #69 names that one, but
eslint-plugin-import and eslint-plugin-react are pinned inside
eslint-config-next and cap at 9 too, so jsx-a11y shipping support is not
on its own enough to lift this. Tracking one would have declared the
hold stale while npm install still failed.

A range carrying a comparator the parser cannot read counts as not
blocking. Three ranges in this lockfile already use forms it does not
read, so the alternative -- treating unreadable as blocked -- would let
the hold outlive an upstream that merely changed comparator style. This
direction can only fail early, and failing early is the cheap direction.

The guard imports stdlib only: CI's script-test job builds a bare
virtualenv, so a third-party import would pass locally and fail there.

Refs #69, #223
EOF
